cases.exposure_context_quote: A 22-year-old male patient of Indian descent, working as a farmer, consumed 500 ml of monocrotophos and an undisclosed quantity of ethanol around 8:30 PM on January 2, 2023.
cases.agent_quote: A 22-year-old male patient of Indian descent, working as a farmer, consumed 500 ml of monocrotophos and an undisclosed quantity of ethanol around 8:30 PM on January 2, 2023.
cases.circumstance: Suicide attempt (ingested monocrotophos and ethanol); text states the case involved a farmer who "ingested monocrotophos and ethanol in a suicide attempt".

symptoms.quote: He encountered two episodes of vomiting, characterized by the expulsion of watery fluid mixed with food particles.

symptoms.finding: tachycardia, hypertension, fever, constricted unresponsive pupils, sluggish deep tendon reflexes, power 3/5 in all four limbs, generalized muscle twitches, weak head-holding
symptoms.quote: The patient presented with a pulse rate of 140 beats per minute, a blood pressure reading of 180/90 mm Hg, a respiratory rate of 25 breaths per minute, and a high fever. ... The Glasgow Coma Scale score was 8 out of 15, and the patient's pupils were constricted and unresponsive in both eyes. Deep tendon reflexes were sluggish, with a power grade of 3/5 in all four limbs, but there was no sensory impairment. Generalized muscle twitches were observed. The patient exhibited weak head-holding

symptoms.finding: intermediate syndrome with prolonged weakness and respiratory paralysis requiring ventilation
symptoms.quote: This report describes the case of a farmer who ingested monocrotophos and ethanol in a suicide attempt, leading to a prolonged stay in the hospital and invasive ventilation, along with complications including ventilator-associated pneumonia.

cases.time_to_care: Initial medical attention at a private hospital; referred to the study institute's emergency department at 3:30 AM on January 3, 2023 (ingestion ~8:30 PM January 2, 2023)

labs.name: hemoglobin
labs.quote: The hemoglobin level was found to be 8.7g/dL, as revealed by the test results.

labs.name: serum AChE day 2
labs.quote: However, the serum AChE levels on day 2 were significantly low, measuring 127.7 U/L, whereas the normal range is 4900-11900 U/L. On day 4, the levels increased to 251.8 U/L.

labs.name: serum AChE day 4
labs.quote: On day 4, the levels increased to 251.8 U/L.

labs.name: ABG pH
labs.quote: The patient's ABG values showed a mixed acidosis with a blood pH of 7.288 and partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO2) of 41.9, alongside right middle-lobe pneumonia.

labs.name: sputum culture
labs.quote: However, sputum samples collected on the morning of day two indicated the presence of Gram-negative bacilli, specifically Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas species.

treatment.name: gastric lavage
treatment.quote: Upon admission, the patient was admitted and underwent gastric lavage.

treatment.name: pralidoxime (four daily doses on day one and day two)
treatment.quote: Intravenous administration of pralidoxime was initiated, with four daily doses on both day one and day two.

treatment.name: atropine (total 9000 mg over 14 days)
treatment.quote: Notably, the patient required an exceptionally high dosage of atropine (9000 mg) over a period of 14 days (Figure 1).

treatment.name: invasive mechanical ventilation
treatment.quote: Invasive mechanical ventilation was initiated in response to the abnormal ABG findings.

treatment.name: IV colistin and ceftriaxone (antibiotics per sensitivity testing)
treatment.quote: Four days after admission, the patient was administered antibiotics based on sensitivity testing, namely IV colistin and ceftriaxone, as well as atropine and pralidoxime.

cases.icu_admission: Yes (invasive mechanical ventilation; explicit ICU wording UNVERIFIED)
cases.outcome: discharged against medical advice on February 5, 2023; alive at discharge
cases.outcome_quote: On February 5, 2023, the patient's family members made a request for discharge against medical advice, which was subsequently approved by the authorities.
cases.sequelae: Persistent inability to swallow requiring Ryle's tube feeding and reliance on external support when sitting at discharge
cases.notes: Sequelae quote: 'Despite these positive indicators, the patient still required Ryle's tube feeding due to his inability to swallow and remained reliant on external support when sitting.' Ventilator-associated pneumonia with Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas; improved limb movements from January until February 5, 2023.
